newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, lifted by light hog marketings, but packer demand was slowing, according to livestock dealers.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota buyers said hogs sold steady, with a top of $58.50 in the country and $59.50 at plants. Illinois buyers said prices were up $0.50, with a top of $58.50 in the country and $59.50 at plants.
Indiana/Ohio buyers said prices were steady to up $0.50 in slow trading, with a top of $54.50 in the country and $57.00 to $58.00 at plants.
Softer wholesale pork prices were trimming demand at some western Corn Belt locations as packers started resisting higher hog prices, the dealers said.
"Packer margins are getting nipped by the higher hog prices and and weak product prices," one southern Minnesota hog buyer said.
Pork carcass cutouts Monday were pegged down $0.18 to $0.27 per cwt as retailers continue to focus on lower priced beef for their advertising features, market sources said.
